# `design/` — Design Sub-Wiki (L2)

## Inclusion test

**Does this describe what a user perceives or does, independent of how it is built?**

If yes, it belongs here. Design holds the experience as specified — journeys, surfaces, components, layout patterns, the design system, the information architecture — and the rationale behind them.

## Layer position

Design is **L2**: it may cite `domain/` and `product/`, and is cited by `engineering/`, `operations/`, `gtm/` and `governance/`.

**Design may not cite `engineering/` or `operations/`** — engineering realizes design, so the citation runs upward from the realization. The pairing is carried from the engineering side instead: `ui-surface-impl` declares `implements:` naming the `ui-surface` it renders as built, and both types attach to the L1 feature by required field.

**Named cost, with a stated resolution:** a design decision constrained by an engineering reality cannot link that constraint. Restate the constraint as an L1 contract fact, or move the decision to an L3 `adr` — or leave it as prose with no link. Do not reach for a downward link.

## In scope

The page types homed here, exhaustively — the boundary, not an illustration of it. The machine-readable copy of the **Page type** column is `page-type-homes.json`, held to this list by a drift guard. The **Subdir** column is held by a different artifact — each type's own template states its home on its `Lives at:` line, and a second guard compares that line against this table. No JSON encodes a subdir; editing one of the two without the other is what the guard reports.

| Subdir | Page type | What goes here |
|---|---|---|
| `journeys/` | `user-journey` | End-to-end experience arcs a persona moves through. It sits below L1 because it *names the task-flows* realizing its stages — a referential fact, not an altitude judgment. |
| `surfaces/` | `ui-surface` | Per-feature surface specs — layout intent, field inventory, actions, states, accessibility. Any visual stays in the design tool or project design file that holds it, linked via `artifacts:`. |
| `components/` | `ui-component` | Reusable component specs — anatomy, variants, states, props, behavior, accessibility. |
| `layout-patterns/` | `layout-pattern` | How a page arranges its regions — regions and landmarks, hierarchy, arrangement per width class, navigation placement. The shell of an application is one. |
| `design-system.md` | `design-system` | The design-system overview — voice and tone, foundations, tokens, component index, interaction patterns, governance. A singleton at the sub-wiki root. |
| `information-architecture/` | `information-architecture` | The sitemap table, navigation model, taxonomy and labeling, wayfinding. A skeleton, a part or an application. |
| `catalogs/` | `catalog` | A design token-group catalog — the governed value set a component or surface resolves against. One page per token group. The icon-set catalog is one too, named by the `design-system` page's `icon-catalog:`. |
| `concepts/` | `concept` | Design principles and mental models — visual hierarchy philosophy, interaction patterns, our accessibility standards. |
| `studies/` | `study` | An investigation of our own surfaces: `method: manual-test` for a usability investigation, `method: variant-prototype` for a side-by-side comparison of structurally different variants of one surface, or `method: card-sort`, `method: tree-test` or `method: click-test` for an information-architecture test — a card sort generates a structure, a tree test evaluates it bare, a click test records first clicks on a rendered page or prototype. A study of an *external* subject is `domain/`. |

**`principles/` is named `concepts/`.** One page type has one folder name across the whole wiki; `concept`'s folder is `concepts/` in every sub-wiki that homes it.

## Explicitly out of scope

- **How it is built** — `engineering/`. `ui-surface` specifies; `ui-surface-impl` implements. Neither links the other: both attach to the L1 `feature` by required field.
- **What is being built and for whom** — `product/`. A `task-flow` is L1; the journey that names several of them is here.
- **Who the user is** — `persona` is `domain/` when the person-type is one the industry has, because that is a fact rather than a choice, and `product/` when our own product definition creates it.
- **A bake-off whose subjects are external** (component libraries, font vendors) — that is a `comparison` in `domain/`. A study of *our* surfaces stays here.
- **A design decision as a standalone record.** There is no design `adr`: the decision lives in the artifact it concerns — a component choice in the `ui-component` page's *Decisions* slot, a surface call in `ui-surface`, a token call in `design-system`, a navigation call in `information-architecture`, a page-arrangement call in `layout-pattern`.

## Owner

The design function owns this sub-wiki. Designers author and maintain principles and accessibility standards, and record each design decision in the page it concerns. Product reads it to understand how product intent is translated into UX. Engineering reads it to implement components and interactions faithfully. Designers reference research findings via cross-wiki links (`[[domain:<path>]]`) when grounding concepts in evidence.

## Mixed origination mode: reasoning and specs originate, a tool's artifacts are linked

Design content divides by where its canonical home is:

**Reasoning and specs originate here.** How we approach design problems — the philosophy behind visual language choices, the rationale for accessibility standards, the mental models behind component decisions — has no better home than this wiki, and neither do the specs built on it: surfaces, components, information architecture, the design system and its token catalogs. They are ideas, reasoning and contracts, not frames. If they live only in a designer's head or a one-off review document, they are invisible to agents and new team members. Originating them here makes them canonical and citable. A project with no design tool keeps its whole design here, in text.

**A tool's artifacts are linked, never copied.** A frame, a story, an icon set or a font that a design tool or component workbench holds stays canonical there; the tool's version history is the record of the visual. Summarizing it here would drift and create false authority, so the wiki links it from the living page it belongs to, and no artifact gets a page of its own. A `file:` artifact is the same pointer to a design file kept in the project, one with no comment syntax and no original in a tool; a design reference with comment syntax names its `ui-surface` or `ui-component` page from its own file with `@prototypes` instead, and an export of a tool-held frame is linked at the frame. Code that realizes the design cites the wiki with `@realizes`; no page links code.

A page's `origination:` field encodes this per page:

- `originate` — the wiki IS canonical. Use for principles, rationale, accessibility standards, brand constraints, surface and component specs, the Decisions registers on `design-system`/`ui-component`/`layout-pattern`/`ui-surface`/`information-architecture` pages, and token catalogs that hold their values. These are authored here and owned here.
- `mirror` — the page records what an external tool holds canonically, with the pointer: a token catalog that follows a design-tool library or a token file under the `tokens/` of the project's design directory (`design.path`), named by its project path, or a brand guide kept in another tool. A page that only links an external artifact keeps its own mode. Prefer `originate` when the content can be authored here.
- `link-only` — metadata and pointer only; no body. No design page type is body-less, so design pages do not declare it.

## Authoring notes

The exact set of subdirs grows as the sub-wiki grows. Create a new subdir when a page type appears for the first time; do not create empty subdirs speculatively.

**Design decisions and analysis fold to living pages.** A design decision is not a standalone `adr` (engineering-only) — it lives in the artifact it concerns: a component choice in the `ui-component` page's **Decisions** slot, a surface call in `ui-surface`, a visual-language or token call in `design-system`, a navigation/taxonomy call in `information-architecture`, a page-arrangement call in `layout-pattern`. Accessibility standards stay `concepts/` pages. A design bake-off over external options is a `comparison` authored in `domain/`; cite it from the decision slot. See [[_authoring:wiki-authorship-routing#routing-table]].

**Artifact pointers fold into the page that describes them.** For `ui-surface`/`ui-component`, the per-surface/-component design-tool frame, or a project file with no comment syntax and no original in a tool (a design reference with comment syntax names its `ui-surface` or `ui-component` page from its own file with `@prototypes` instead), is carried in the dedicated `artifacts:` frontmatter field (a `"kind:target"` dash-list; a `file:` entry takes a path relative to the project root) — these are `curated` living specs, not `link-only` stubs. Other artifacts — a design-tool library, a component workbench, a font or a brand file — are linked from the living page they belong to: `design-system` for system-wide libraries, fonts and brand, `catalog` for token groups and for an icon set, which the `design-system` page names in `icon-catalog:`. A catalog that records what such a library holds declares `origination: mirror`; the `design-system` page that links the library keeps `originate`. A one-off artifact with no natural home lists under `design-system` `## Related`. Either way the pixels stay canonical in the tool, never summarized here; there is no standalone `mirror-source` stub in design.

## Cross-cutting UX standards

Design-adjacent standards have distinct, non-overlapping homes — author each once and reference it:

- **Accessibility** — the WCAG contract: contrast, focus order, keyboard operation, screen-reader semantics. A design concern that **originates here** (see Owner) as `concepts/` pages. Other sub-wikis reference `[[design:concepts/<slug>]]`; do not re-author it elsewhere.
- **Resilience** — how a surface handles empty / loading / error / partial / access-gated states. A **product-owned** behavioral standard; design references it as `[[product:concepts/app-ux-resilience]]` (or the project's resilience standard), not re-authored here.
- **Voice & tone** — microcopy, labeling conventions, and content style. The design-system overview's own `Voice and tone` section (`[[design:design-system#voice-and-tone]]`), not a `concepts/` page. `ui-component`'s Content-guidelines section and `ui-surface`'s guidance point at it rather than restate it.

## Templates to use

Design pages draw from two sources. Most use the design-specific shapes that ship as **local** page-templates under `_templates/`, deployed into `<wiki.location>/design/_templates/` so they travel with the sub-wiki. The rest come from the shared `_templates/` pool; the table marks which.

| Template | Source | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| `_templates/concept.md` | shared pool | `concepts/` pages |
| `_templates/study.md` | shared pool | `studies/` pages (`method: manual-test`, `variant-prototype`, `card-sort`, `tree-test` or `click-test`) |
| `_templates/catalog.md` | shared pool | `catalogs/` pages (`catalog` — token-group and icon-set value sets) |
| `_templates/user-journey.md` | design-local | `journeys/` pages (`user-journey`) |
| `_templates/ui-surface.md` | design-local | `surfaces/<module>/` pages (`ui-surface`) |
| `_templates/ui-component.md` | design-local | `components/` pages (`ui-component`) |
| `_templates/layout-pattern.md` | design-local | `layout-patterns/` pages (`layout-pattern`) |
| `_templates/design-system.md` | design-local | `design-system.md` singleton (`design-system`) |
| `_templates/information-architecture.md` | design-local | `information-architecture/` pages (`information-architecture`) |

To create a new page:

1. Copy the relevant template from `_templates/` into the appropriate subdir (the table above marks which are shared-pool vs design-local).
2. Rename to `kebab-case.md` matching the page title.
3. Substitute placeholders: `{{TITLE}}`, `{{DATE}}`, `{{OWNER}}`, `{{CONFIDENCE}}`, plus any type-specific placeholders. **Exception:** the design-local page-templates (`user-journey`, `ui-surface`, `ui-component`, `layout-pattern`, `design-system`, `information-architecture`) fix `owner: design` by construction and omit `{{OWNER}}` — do not substitute it. Several of them also carry required type-specific frontmatter; the template's own `Extra frontmatter:` line is the list, and it is the one that stays correct as a type gains a field. Fill each with the real page reference rather than leaving the scaffolded `<placeholder>` — a leftover is an audit error.
4. Set `origination:` to `originate`, or to `mirror` for a page that records what a design-tool library holds (see above).
5. Fill the body; leave section headers even when a section is empty (use "None." or remove only if the template explicitly says to).
6. Append a `log.md` entry: `## [YYYY-MM-DD] <op> | <title>`.

For artifact pointers: `ui-surface` and `ui-component` pages record the design-tool frame pointer, or the project path of a project file with no comment syntax and no original in a tool, in the `artifacts:` frontmatter field, a dash-list of `"kind:target"` entries; `design-system` and `catalog` record theirs in `sources:` or the body. The rule behind both, and which artifact kind goes where, is the fold note under **Artifact pointers fold into the page that describes them** above. Note that `sources:` otherwise means derivation provenance (`_raw/` snapshots, source URLs).

## What an engine checks, and what it does not

Rules in this file fall into the classes below, and the file does not otherwise distinguish them.

- **Checked, and an error.** Cross-wiki link resolution and the layer order (`/wiki-lint`), and a page's structure against its template — sections, declared table columns, block bullets, leftover placeholders (`/wiki-conformance-audit`). These fail a run and name the page.
- **Checked upstream, against the framework rather than your page.** The type list and the Subdir column in the table above are held to their sources by drift guards that run in agent-kit's own suite, not here. You see them as a failing build in that repo, never as a finding on your wiki.
- **Not read by any engine.** The default origination mode this README states is authoring guidance, not a value anything applies to a page: a page that sets no `origination:` is never flagged for disagreeing with the default. The same is true of which subdir a page of a multi-home type belongs in, and of every cell value inside a table whose columns are checked. These are review's job.

Run the two commands for the live list; neither this section nor any other file enumerates the checks, because a list maintained beside the thing it describes is the drift this wiki keeps closing.

## Retiring or relocating a page

Neither is a hand edit, and they are different operations.

- **Retiring** a page that others cite — run `/wiki-archive`. One invocation moves the page under `_archive/`, writes the `redirect` stub at the old path so every existing link still resolves, rebuilds `index.md` and the reverse citation index, and appends the `log.md` line. Follow it with `/wiki-lint`. Never write the stub by hand: `_templates/redirect-stub.md` is the scaffold for repairing a damaged stub, and a hand-copied one names an `_archive/` path nothing moved anything to while the original page stays live — two answers at two addresses.
- **Relocating** a page that is not being retired — run `/wiki-move`. It repoints the incoming links and leaves **no** stub, because a stub for a page that still exists is a second, stale answer to the same question.

Splitting and merging carry page-local ids across; the rules are in [[_authoring:wiki-page-ids#splitting-and-merging]].

## Cross-wiki reference syntax

Design's allowed outbound set is `domain/` and `product/` — every layer above it. It may not cite `engineering/`, `operations/`, `gtm/` or `governance/`.

- **Referencing design content from another sub-wiki:**
  - Concepts: `[[design:concepts/<slug>]]`
  - Surfaces: `[[design:surfaces/<module>/<feature-slug>]]`
  - Components: `[[design:components/<component-slug>]]`, or `[[design:components/<module>/<component-slug>]]` for a component under its module
  - Layout patterns: `[[design:layout-patterns/<pattern-slug>]]`
  - Design system: `[[design:design-system]]` — singleton; no trailing path
  - Information architecture: `[[design:information-architecture/<scope-slug>]]`
- **Referencing within the design sub-wiki:** omit the prefix — `[[concepts/<slug>]]`, `[[components/<slug>]]`
- **Anchor syntax:** `[[design:concepts/visual-hierarchy#spacing]]` — anchor matches a header slug in the target page

These are the forms most often cited across a sub-wiki boundary, not one row per directory: the link form is mechanical — `[[design:<path-to-page>]]` — and the template table above is the complete map of which type lives in which directory. A directory with no row here is cited exactly the same way, and every sub-wiki README follows this pattern rather than indexing itself.

`/wiki-lint` validates all cross-wiki links when it is run — before a PR, or on a cadence. A broken link **or an out-of-hierarchy reference** is a lint error, not a commit block: nothing here is wired to a hook ([[_authoring:wiki-conventions#cross-reference-protocol]]).

## Typical raw sources

Content flowing into `_raw/` that this sub-wiki processes:

- Design reviews and critique session notes
- User research outputs that inform UX or interaction patterns (primary landing in `domain/`; cross-referenced from here)
- Brand guidelines documents and brand refresh decks
- Accessibility audit results and WCAG compliance reviews
- Component library migration notes and deprecation decisions
- Design system documentation from previous versions being migrated into principles

Raw sources land under `<wiki.location>/_raw/` — the shared pool for the whole project. A single raw source may underpin pages in multiple sub-wikis. Cite back to the named sources via the `sources:` frontmatter field on all `derived` pages.

## When to originate vs mirror

- **Originate** when the content is reasoning or a spec, not an artifact. A principle explaining *why* visual hierarchy is applied a certain way belongs here — there is no frame for a mental model. When the insight would otherwise live only in a review document or a designer's memory, originate it.
- **Mirror** when an external tool holds the canonical content and the page records what it holds: a token catalog that follows a design-tool library or a token file under the `tokens/` of the project's design directory (`design.path`), named by its project path, or a brand guide kept in a team document. Prefer an `originate` page that distills the canonical claims when the source is stable enough to allow it.
- **Link, never page,** when the content is an artifact a tool holds by necessity — a frame URL, a story, an icon set download link: record the pointer on the page it belongs to.

Principles, rationale and accessibility standards belong in the wiki even when they reference external tools.

Some of what a page must say is not settled when it is written, and the grammar distinguishes the ways that can be true rather than collapsing them. A page whose SUBJECT has a lifecycle carries a typed `status:`. A section whose content arrives at a named later event is declared on the template's `Appends:` line and reads `Pending: <that event>.` until it does — never `None.`, which says the author considered it and had nothing to say. A page that is a register of items with their own states carries those states as columns. Which one applies is the template's to declare, not yours to choose; the full grammar is [[_authoring:wiki-page-state#page-state-axes]].
